approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `value` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

coverBadDebt(uint256).details: This function is callable by an admin/keeper role. It calculates the shortfall between the total debt and the current value of the collateral, then requests that amount from the Insurance Fund. The position is then closed.

params.positionId: The ID of the position to cover.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

params.mintAmount: Amount of stablecoin to mint (must be properly collateralized)

returns.positionId: The ID of the newly created position

returns.remaining: Amount user can still withdraw today
Amount user can still mint against this position

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleGranted} event.

returns._0: isHealthy True if position is healthy

name().details: Returns the name of the token.

pause().details: Only PAUSER_ROLE can pause. Used to stop minting and liquidations during emergencies

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

proxiableUUID().details: Implementation of the ERC-1822 {proxiableUUID} function. This returns the storage slot used by the implementation. It is used to validate the implementation's compatibility when performing an upgrade. IMPORTANT: A proxy pointing at a proxiable contract should not be considered proxiable itself, because this risks bricking a proxy that upgrades to it, by delegating to itself until out of gas. Thus it is critical that this function revert if invoked through a proxy. This is guaranteed by the `notDelegated` modifier.

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been revoked `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `callerConfirmation`. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

requestZMWWithdrawal(uint256,string).details: Burns dcUSD, locks exchange rate, emits event for off-chain processorOff-chain service handles actual mobile money transfer via MTN/Airtel/Zamtel APIs

params.dcUSDAmount: Amount of dcUSD to burn and convert to ZMW
params.mobileMoneyAccount: Mobile money phone number (e.g., "+260977123456" for Zambia)

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

params.newFee: New origination fee amount (in dcUSD, 18 decimals)

params.newDailyLimit: New daily withdrawal limit per user

params._processor: Address of authorized off-chain withdrawal service

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `value`.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Skips emitting an {Approval} event indicating an allowance update. This is not required by the ERC. See {xref-ERC20-_approve-address-address-uint256-bool-}[_approve]. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `value`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `value`.

unpause().details: Only DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can unpause. Requires careful review before unpausing

upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes).details: Upgrade the implementation of the proxy to `newImplementation`, and subsequently execute the function call encoded in `data`. Calls {_authorizeUpgrade}. Emits an {Upgraded} event.

closePosition(uint256).notice: Close position by burning all debt and withdrawing collateral

coverBadDebt(uint256).notice: Covers bad debt for an underwater position after a failed auction.

depositAndMint(bytes32,uint256).notice: Deposit Dead Capital asset as collateral and mint stablecoin

getCollateralRatio(uint256).notice: Get current collateral ratio for a position

getMaxMintableAmount(bytes32).notice: Get maximum mintable amount for an asset (with buffer applied)

getPositionHealth(uint256).notice: Get position details with current health metrics

getRemainingDailyZMWLimit(address).notice: Get user's remaining daily ZMW withdrawal limit

getRemainingMintCapacity(uint256).notice: Get remaining minting capacity for an existing position

getUserPositions(address).notice: Get all positions for a user

isPositionHealthy(uint256).notice: Check if position is healthy (above warning threshold)

mintMore(uint256,uint256).notice: Mint additional stablecoin against existing position

pause().notice: Emergency pause mechanism - halts all critical operations

requestZMWWithdrawal(uint256,string).notice: Request ZMW withdrawal to mobile money account

unpause().notice: Unpause the contract - resumes normal operations

updateCollateralValue(uint256).notice: Update collateral value from oracle (for revaluation)
